title: Plural of common -in words
summary: For these -in words, use the strong form and replace -in with -imia/-imiä: puhelin (“telephone”) → puhelimia.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

These -in words use a vowel stem ending in -ime- in other cases. In the plural partitive, that becomes -imi- before -a/-ä. A stem is the part of a word used before an ending. Learn the strong stem shown in each example: some dictionary forms have a single t that becomes tt in this plural form. Spelling -in alone does not establish membership of this family.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

commonMistakes: Use -imia/-imiä, not the unchanged singular -inta/-intä form.
Use soitt- and keitt- in soittimia and keittimiä.
Keep vowel harmony from the complete word.
